schemaNote: GPIR Global Announcements intelligence records. Each record traces a ticker item to a real, named, verifiable source with an original publication URL wherever status is not SOURCE_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED. Never fabricate a source URL: an item without a reliably identified primary source is published with status SOURCE_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED and source:null instead of an invented link. "organisation" holds the regulator/institution/company the record is actually about, which may differ from source.name (the outlet that published it, e.g. an official press agency reporting a central bank's decision). "lastUpdated" is set only when a previously published record is materially revised (see governance note in trust-engine.js); it must never silently overwrite the original publishedDate. Top-level "lastRefreshed" records the last manually validated dataset refresh; no scheduled ingestion mechanism is currently deployed.

records.title: UAE Central Bank Payment Token Services Regulation moves into operational phase
records.tickerHeadline: Central Bank of the UAE payment token regulation now fully operational

source.name: Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE)
source.publicationTitle: Payment Token Services Regulation — CBUAE Rulebook

records.summary: The Central Bank of the UAE's Payment Token Services Regulation, which licenses and supervises the issuance, conversion, custody and transfer of fiat-referenced payment tokens including stablecoins, moved out of its transition period on 16 June 2026 and is now in its operational phase.
records.whyItMatters: The regulation gives UAE-licensed payment token issuers and service providers a formal supervisory framework — a reference point for stablecoin activity in a major Gulf payments hub, with direct relevance to cross-border settlement using tokenised value.
records.headline: UAE Central Bank Payment Token Services Regulation moves into operational phase

records.title: Saudi Central Bank licenses Malaa Company under its Open Banking Framework
records.tickerHeadline: SAMA licenses first account-information provider under Open Banking Framework

source.name: Saudi Press Agency (SPA), reporting a Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) licensing decision
source.publicationTitle: SAMA Licenses Malaa Company for Information Technology to Provide Open Banking Services

records.summary: The Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) licensed Malaa Company for Information Technology to provide payment account information services, one of the regulated activities under SAMA's Open Banking Framework, which SAMA moved from a supervised sandbox into a formally licensed activity in March 2026.
records.whyItMatters: Formal licensing of account-information providers is a required step before open banking services can operate commercially in Saudi Arabia, directly affecting how banks, PSPs and fintechs may share payment account data under the Kingdom's Vision 2030 digital payments agenda.
records.headline: Saudi Central Bank licenses Malaa Company under its Open Banking Framework
records.sourceName: Saudi Press Agency (SPA), reporting a Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) licensing decision

records.title: Favara-UPI cross-border payment corridor goes live between Maldives and India
records.tickerHeadline: Favara-UPI cross-border corridor goes live between Maldives and India

source.name: Maldives Monetary Authority (MMA), reported via India's official press service
source.publicationTitle: Favara-UPI Cross-Border Payment Corridor Goes Live Between Maldives and India

records.summary: The Maldives Monetary Authority announced that its domestic instant payment system, Favara, is now interoperable with India's UPI, enabling real-time person-to-person transfers from Maldivian Rufiyaa to Indian Rupees. The corridor launched with two participating Maldivian banks, Bank of Maldives and Maldives Islamic Bank, following an integration agreement between NPCI International Payments Limited and the MMA signed in July 2025.
records.whyItMatters: This extends UPI's cross-border interoperability to another live corridor, a stated RBI / NPCI International priority, and gives Indian expatriates and Maldivian residents a formal instant-payment remittance rail for family-maintenance and gift transfers.
records.headline: Favara-UPI cross-border payment corridor goes live between Maldives and India
records.sourceName: Maldives Monetary Authority (MMA), reported via India's official press service
keywords: Maldives Monetary Authority (MMA), reported via India's official press service

records.title: Reserve Bank of India publishes 'Payments Vision 2028'
records.summary: The RBI published its 'Payments Vision 2028' roadmap, themed 'Shaping India's Payment Frontier', setting out initiatives through December 2028 including an interoperability framework for Trade Receivables Discounting Systems, a universal on/off switch for digital payment instruments, and streamlined cross-border payment authorisation under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act and FEMA.
records.whyItMatters: As RBI's successor to earlier Payments Vision documents, this sets regulatory direction for India's digital payments ecosystem through 2028, including how cross-border payment authorisation will be streamlined.
records.headline: Reserve Bank of India publishes 'Payments Vision 2028'

records.title: MAS and ABS chart PayNow 'Generation 2' instant payment enhancements
records.tickerHeadline: MAS and ABS chart PayNow 'Generation 2' instant payment study
records.organisation: Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS)

source.name: Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS)
source.publicationTitle: MAS and ABS Chart Instant Payments Enhancements with PayNow Generation 2 Study

records.summary: MAS and the Association of Banks in Singapore announced they will study four areas of enhancement to Singapore's PayNow instant payment infrastructure under a 'PayNow Generation 2' initiative, announced at the ABS Annual Dinner on 25 June 2026.
records.whyItMatters: PayNow is Singapore's core retail instant-payment rail; enhancements here affect how consumers, merchants and public agencies transact domestically and set direction for Singapore's broader instant-payments interoperability with regional schemes.
records.headline: MAS and ABS chart PayNow 'Generation 2' instant payment enhancements

records.title: Swift launches cross-border payments scheme for consumer-originated transfers
records.tickerHeadline: Swift launches consumer cross-border payments scheme with 40+ banks

source.name: Swift
source.publicationTitle: Swift accelerates transformation of consumer payments as banks roll out new framework for retail transactions

records.summary: Swift, working with more than 40 banks, launched the Swift Payments Scheme — a set of enforceable rules intended to make cross-border consumer-originated payments faster, more predictable and more transparent. More than 70 financial institutions committed to implementing the scheme in 2026 across corridors including Australia, Bangladesh, Canada, China, Germany, India, Pakistan, Spain, Thailand, the UK and the US.
records.whyItMatters: As the dominant global messaging network for cross-border payments, a Swift-led rulebook for consumer remittance corridors has outsized influence on settlement speed and transparency standards banks apply to retail cross-border transfers, including several major remittance-receiving markets.
records.headline: Swift launches cross-border payments scheme for consumer-originated transfers

records.title: Mastercard expands settlement capabilities to include regulated stablecoins
records.tickerHeadline: Mastercard expands card settlement to include regulated stablecoins

source.name: Mastercard
source.publicationTitle: Mastercard expands settlement capabilities to include stablecoin settlement

records.summary: Mastercard announced expanded settlement capabilities, adding intraday, weekend and holiday card settlement and on-chain settlement using regulated stablecoins including USDC, PYUSD, USDG and RLUSD across eight blockchain networks. ARQ, CBW Bank, Cross River, Lead Bank and Nuvei were named among the first participants.
records.whyItMatters: Stablecoin settlement support from a major card network signals growing integration between traditional card rails and blockchain-based settlement, with direct relevance to settlement speed, weekend/holiday liquidity and the regulated stablecoin ecosystem.
records.headline: Mastercard expands settlement capabilities to include regulated stablecoins

records.title: Mastercard completes acquisition of BVNK to advance stablecoin infrastructure
records.tickerHeadline: Mastercard completes acquisition of stablecoin infrastructure firm BVNK

source.name: Mastercard
source.publicationTitle: Mastercard completes acquisition of BVNK to advance global stablecoin capabilities

records.summary: Mastercard completed its acquisition of stablecoin infrastructure company BVNK, adding BVNK's stablecoin payment and settlement infrastructure to Mastercard's global payments network.
records.whyItMatters: This is one of the clearest signals yet of a major card network directly acquiring stablecoin infrastructure rather than only partnering, consolidating stablecoin settlement, issuance and payments capability inside an incumbent network.
records.headline: Mastercard completes acquisition of BVNK to advance stablecoin infrastructure

records.title: FATF opens consultation on strengthened payment-transparency standards
records.tickerHeadline: FATF opens consultation on strengthened payment-transparency standards

source.name: Financial Action Task Force (FATF)
source.publicationTitle: FATF launches public consultation on guidance to increase payment transparency

records.summary: FATF opened a public consultation on new guidance supporting its strengthened Recommendation 16 standards on payment transparency, agreed in June 2025, which require more information to accompany cross-border payments and tools to protect against fraud and error. Countries are expected to implement the changes by the end of 2030.
records.whyItMatters: Recommendation 16 is the global AML/CFT baseline for what information must travel with a cross-border payment; this consultation will shape how banks and PSPs worldwide implement payment-transparency and fraud-prevention requirements over the coming years.
records.headline: FATF opens consultation on strengthened payment-transparency standards
